skill.name: scientific-visualization
skill.description: Create publication-ready scientific figures with Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly guidance for journal formats, accessibility, layout, and export settings.
skill.summary: Create journal-ready scientific figures with accessible palettes, layout guidance, and publication export settings.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: AI review found extensive static-analysis noise from Markdown code fences, plotting documentation, palette comments, and dictionary keys() calls. One real medium-risk behavior remains: scripts/style_presets.py can write a Matplotlib style file to a caller-supplied path.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted output path for generated Matplotlib style files.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain output_file to a safe project directory, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and avoid overwriting existing files unless the user explicitly confirms.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Using jet/rainbow colormap**: Not perceptually uniform; avoid
- Avoid abbreviations unless space-constrained (define in caption)
3. **Chart junk**: Unnecessary grid lines, 3D effects, decorations
Apply journal-specific styles using the matplotlib style files in `assets/`:
3. For diverging data, use colorblind-safe diverging map (`RdBu_r`, `PuOr`)
- `save_publication_figure()`: Save in multiple formats with correct DPI
- `apply_publication_style()`: Apply preset styles (default, nature, science, cell)
- Run directly: `python scripts/style_presets.py` to see examples

medium_findings.title: Python file write/append
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper opens output_file with write mode, so a caller can create or overwrite an arbitrary path. It appears intended for style-file generation, but it is still real filesystem write capability.

content.value_statement: Scientific figures often fail journal checks for size, resolution, color, and labels. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create accessible publication-ready figures.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of publication figures with Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly.
Applies journal-oriented sizing, fonts, line widths, and export formats.
Recommends colorblind-safe palettes and perceptually uniform colormaps.
Supports multi-panel layouts, panel labels, error bars, and significance markers.
Provides helper scripts for saving PDF, EPS, TIFF, PNG, and SVG outputs.
Checks figure dimensions against common journal column requirements.
limitations: Does not validate the scientific correctness of input data or statistical tests.
Requires the relevant Python plotting libraries to be installed by the user.
Journal requirements can change, so final author instructions should be checked.
Static Plotly export may need extra local dependencies such as Kaleido.

use_cases.title: Prepare Manuscript Figures
use_cases.description: Convert analysis plots into journal-ready figures with correct dimensions, labels, fonts, and export formats.

use_cases.title: Improve Figure Accessibility
use_cases.description: Replace weak color choices with colorblind-safe palettes and grayscale-friendly encodings.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Visuals
use_cases.description: Apply consistent plotting styles across manuscripts, posters, supplementary figures, and presentations.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Basic Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single publication plot.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a publication-ready line plot from my data. Use clear axis labels with units, a colorblind-safe palette, and export settings for a manuscript figure.

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Existing Plot
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a draft figure before submission.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current scientific plot for journal readiness. Recommend changes for size, fonts, colors, labels, legends, resolution, and file format.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Panel Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine several analyses into one figure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-panel figure for a manuscript. Include consistent styling, panel labels, aligned axes, error bars, and export settings for a double-column layout.

prompt_templates.title: Target a Specific Journal
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare my figure workflow for a Nature-style submission. Specify dimensions, font sizes, line widths, color choices, file formats, and final quality checks.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for a manuscript-ready line plot with error bars.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a plotting plan with figure size, labels, accessible palette choices, uncertainty display guidance, and export recommendations.

output_examples.input: A student has a draft heatmap that uses a rainbow color map.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a perceptually uniform color map, a labeled colorbar, readable tick labels, and grayscale review steps.

output_examples.input: A lab wants one figure with four related panels.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a consistent multi-panel layout with panel letters, spacing, shared style rules, and journal-ready export formats.

best_practices: State the target journal, final figure width, and required output formats before plotting.
Use colorblind-safe palettes and redundant encodings such as markers or line styles.
Check final-size readability, axis units, error bar definitions, and grayscale interpretation.
anti_patterns: Using rainbow or red-green palettes for scientific meaning without accessibility checks.
Exporting plots as low-resolution JPEG files for publication submission.
Mixing fonts, sizes, colors, and line widths across panels in one manuscript.

faq.question: Which plotting libraries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly workflows for scientific figures.

faq.question: Can it create figures for specific journals?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for common Nature, Science, Cell, PLOS, ACS, and IEEE requirements.

faq.question: Does it choose accessible colors?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends colorblind-safe palettes, grayscale checks, and perceptually uniform colormaps.

faq.question: Can it export print-ready files?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper scripts support common publication formats such as PDF, EPS, TIFF, PNG, and SVG.

faq.question: Does it run statistical tests?
faq.answer: No. It helps display uncertainty and significance clearly, but it does not validate statistical methods.

faq.question: Is final journal compliance guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Authors should compare final figures with the current instructions from the target journal.
